purpose: decide deliberately which technical debt to repay, defer or accept, using cost and risk rather than irritation
entry_criteria: Known debt items are collected from engineers, incidents and reviews
Delivery and incident data are available
A planning forum with the owner exists
inputs: list of debt items with locations
procedure: List debt items with the problem, where it lives and what it costs (slows delivery, causes defects, blocks changes, creates risk).
Estimate the cost of carrying each item and the effort to repay it; use data such as change frequency and incident links.
Rank by value of repayment, not by how disliked an item is; debt in code nobody changes can wait.
Decide per item: repay now, schedule, defer with a trigger, or accept; record the reason.
Put repayment items in the backlog with an owner and a definition of done.
Review the register each quarter and retire items that are no longer relevant.
acceptance_criteria: Each item has a cost, an effort and a decision
Ranking uses data, not only opinion
Deferred items have a trigger or a review date
validation_method: Product owner and architect agreement on priorities.

validation.command: git log --since='6 months ago' --name-only --pretty=format: -- src/billing | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head   # example
validation.expect: change hotspots recorded in the register

validation.check: check each repay item has a backlog link and an owner

failure_modes.detection: Register has hundreds of vague items
Items older than a year with no decision

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: The billing module appears in 40 percent of the last quarter's incidents and is changed weekly, so its fragile date handling is ranked first and scheduled; an ugly but stable report generator is accepted.
